transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I've just been feeling tired all the time and I've no energy. It's been coming on gradually over about two months now, and it's getting me down.
Can you tell me how this tiredness is affecting your day-to-day life, if at all, and whether you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?

It's affecting most things, really. I'm tired all day, worse in the afternoons, and I've started needing a nap most days, which I never used to do — my energy's about a 3 out of 10, and I've had to stop my twice-weekly swimming. I'm also struggling to help my husband wash and dress in the mornings.

As for medicines, codeine makes me very sick, so I avoid it.

Can you tell me about any medicines you take — regular ones or anything new or changed recently, and the dose if you know it — and also any past health problems, operations, or hospital stays you've had?

I take metformin 500 mg twice a day for my diabetes, levothyroxine 100 micrograms each morning for my thyroid, and omeprazole 20 mg once a day for indigestion — I've been on that for years. I also take ibuprofen 400 mg that I buy from the chemist most days for shoulder pain. Nothing new or changed recently.

As for my health, I've had type 2 diabetes for 12 years and an underactive thyroid. I've not had any operations or hospital stays.
Could you tell me more about this tiredness—where you feel it in your body, if anywhere, and what makes it better or worse?

It's not in one particular place — it's just a whole-body tiredness, like I've got nothing in the tank. It's worse in the afternoon, and a nap does help a bit, but I still wake up not feeling refreshed even after about seven hours' sleep. I've also noticed I get more short of breath than usual going up hills.
Is there anything else you've noticed alongside the tiredness that you'd like to add?
Friends have said I look pale, and my mood feels a bit flat with all the caring. I've not had any chest pain, no weight loss, and no change in my bowels.
What, if anything, worries you most about how you've been feeling?
What worries me most is that I won't be able to keep caring for my husband. He has Parkinson's and I'm the main one looking after him, and I'm already struggling with the mornings.
Is there anything else you take for your health—like medicines, vitamins, or supplements—that we haven’t talked about yet?
No, that's everything — just the metformin, levothyroxine, omeprazole and the ibuprofen. I don't take any vitamins or supplements.
You've mentioned diabetes and an underactive thyroid—is there anything else about your health in the past that you think I should know about?
No, that's all — just the diabetes and the underactive thyroid. There's nothing else I can think of.
Along with the tiredness, is there anything else you've noticed that we haven't talked about yet?
I don't think so — I've told you about the breathlessness on hills, looking pale, the flat mood, and waking unrefreshed. There's nothing else I've noticed.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
